newsitem.title: UK: UK govt caps spending of three local authorities.
newsitem.headline: UK govt caps spending of three local authorities.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government on Thursday ordered three local authorities -- Oxfordshire, Somerset and Warwickshire county councils -- to cut their budgets.
Deputy Prime Minister John Prescott said the three had been designated for "capping" and would be required to reduce their spending unless they could convince the government otherwise.
"This decision demonstrates that we are taking our commitments on spending very seriously," he said in a reply to a parliamentary question.
Prescott said the vast majority of the country's 436 authorities had set budgets and council taxes within limits laid down by his Conservative predecessor.

As far as the three exceptions were concerned, he said, "I have proposed caps for them which I consider, on the basis of all the information available so far, to be reasonable and achievable in all the circumstances of the authorities concerned."
The authorities now have 28 days to decide whether to accept or reject the proposed cap.
If any of them challenge the ruling, they must propose and justify an alternative budget.
The Local Government Finance Act of 1992 allows the government to cap authorities whose budget requirements are, in its opinion, excessive or represent an excessive increase over the previous year.
